passage:
A news report showed a floating farm built on water. It grew vegetables in a city where land was limited.
In class, students discussed whether floating farms were a good idea. Some liked that they used unused space. Others worried about cost, storms, and water pollution.
Their teacher said new ideas should be tested with both hope and doubt. Hope helps people try. Doubt helps people ask useful questions.
The students designed their own model farms with rules for safety and waste.
The floating farm was not just a strange invention. It became a lesson in problem-solving: when land, food, and cities change, people must imagine new ways to grow.
